summary: Akira Shimada works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and doctoral supervisor Daud Ali. He held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1957–1962), where he served as an assistant (~1962–1967) and associate professor (1991–1994). He also lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University, served as assistant (1961) and professor (1965–1991) at the University of Tokyo, and became professor emeritus at Meikai University.

Akira Unete is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His career includes appointments at Otani University, where he served as an associate professor (attested 2010) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Akira Hirakawa, Naoshiro Tsuji, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at ANU, directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and taught at Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as an adviser at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he served as abbot (attested 2009).
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran is an Indologist. Parmeswaran pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026) and held a research post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Akshay Ramanlal Desai (1915–1994) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai from circa 1938 to 1946, working under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye between approximately 1940 and 1946.
Alan Avdagić is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Avdagić worked as a research associate at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2026) and held a post at the University of Würzburg.
Alan Entwistle (1949–1996) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his education at the University of Southampton and at SOAS University of London (~1974–1982).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Sinology. After completing his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988), he held academic posts at the University of Delaware, including professor in 1992 and associate professor of philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2008) under supervisor Parimal G. Patil, and also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans (1923–2001) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He completed studies at the University of Toronto (1946) and Princeton University (1948, 1950).

Alan Lomax (1915–2002) completed his education at St. Mark's School of Texas, Choate Rosemary Hall, Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1934–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).

Alan Sponberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia and held faculty positions at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and Stanford University's Department of Religious Studies (attested 1988).

Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seabury-Western Theological Seminary, served as Northwestern University's chaplain (1944–1950), taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957), and held a Harvard fellowship (1962–1964).

Alasdair Urquhart (born 1945) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (MA) and the University of Pittsburgh (PhD). He taught as an assistant professor at University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at Toronto (1986).

Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013). He has served at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2015), SOAS (attested 2019), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer, Alfred Körte, Friedrich Leo, and Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships and teaching posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, Bern, and Basel.
